{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Enemies of the United States are determined to acquire and use biological and chemical weapons.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Terrorists may use genetically engineered bioweapons incorporating anthrax, ebola, smallpox, sarin, or ricin.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Such weapons are capable of inflicting grievous harm on any nation caught unprepared.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"President George W. Bush made bolstering the nation's defenses against bioterrorism a central focus of his Administration.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The federal bioterrorism budget increased by more than 1,600 percent, from $294 million in 2001 to $5.2 billion in 2004.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Bioterror research expanded by more than 3,100 percent, from $53 million in 2001 to $1.7 billion in 2005.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The size of the Strategic National Stockpile of vaccines and countermeasures increased by 50 percent since 2001.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"More than $5.5 billion was secured to enhance the stockpile and to encourage the development of new vaccines and countermeasures.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[5]},{"claim_text":"President Bush's commitment to building up the biological defenses of the United States has made the nation less vulnerable to bioterrorism than it was three years ago.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[6]},{"claim_text":"President Bush's continuing commitment to implement further biodefense projects holds the promise of an even more secure future.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[6]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
